question: Wherein consists the sinfulness of that Estate whereinto Man fell?
answer: The sinfulness of that Estate whereinto Man fell, consists in the Guilt of Adam's first Sin, the want of Original Righteousness, and the Corruption of his whole Nature, which is commonly called Original Sin; together with all actual Transgressions which proceed from it.

question: What doth the Preface to the Ten Commandments teach us?
answer: The Preface to the Ten Commandments teacheth us, that because God is the LORD, and our God, and Redeemer, therefore we are bound to keep all his Commandments.
right_choice: Because God is the LORD, our God, and Redeemer, therefore we are bound to keep all his Commandments
wrong_choices: God's Commandments are given to us so we may earn His grace | We are advised but not bound to keep all of God's Commandments | God requires us to keep some Commandments because He is just and holy
audit_why: No fault found.

question: What is required in the first Commandment?
answer: The first Commandment requireth us, to know and acknowledge God to be the only true God, and our God; and to worship and glorify him accordingly.
right_choice: To know and acknowledge God as the only true God, and to worship and glorify him
wrong_choices: To believe that God exists and to pray and read Scripture daily | To choose God as our personal Savior and commit our lives to serving him | To honor God above all things and to obey all his Commandments
audit_why: No fault found.

question: What are we specially taught by these words "before me" in the first Commandment?
answer: These words "before me" in the first Commandment, teach us, that God who seeth all things, taketh notice of, and is much displeased with the Sin of having any other God.
right_choice: That God sees all things and is displeased with having any other god.
wrong_choices: That the first Commandment requires us to honor God in everything | That we must keep God always before us in our minds and hearts | That God alone deserves our worship and praise above all creatures
audit_why: No fault found.

question: What is required in the second Commandment?
answer: The second Commandment requireth, the receiving, observing, and keeping pure and entire all such religious Worship and Ordinances, as God hath appointed in his Word.
right_choice: The receiving, observing, and keeping pure and entire all such religious Worship and Ordinances as God appointed
wrong_choices: The keeping holy to God of such set times as he appointed in his Word | The knowing and acknowledging of God to be the only true God, and our God | The holy and reverent use of God's Names, Titles, Attributes, Ordinances, Word, and Works
audit_why: Two wrong choices were only loose rewordings of the right answer, so I replaced all three with what the catechism says the first, third and fourth Commandments require.

question: What is forbidden in the second Commandment?
answer: The second Commandment forbiddeth the worshipping of God by Images, or any other Way not appointed in his Word.
right_choice: The worshipping of God by Images, or any other Way not appointed in his Word
wrong_choices: The taking of God's name in vain by oaths or careless speech | The breaking of idols and the refusal to worship any images at all | The working of any labour on the Lord's Day, the day of rest
audit_why: Two wrong choices were also right, since one repeated the answer in other words and another was close to it, so I replaced them with wrong choices drawn from the third and fourth Commandments.

question: What are the Reasons annexed to the second Commandment?
answer: The Reasons annexed to the second Commandment are, God's Sovereignty over us, his Propriety in us, and the Zeal he has to his own Worship.
right_choice: God's Sovereignty over us, his Propriety in us, and the Zeal he has to his own Worship
wrong_choices: God's Rest on the seventh day, his Blessing on it, and his Example to us | God's Mercy to us, his Patience with us, and the Glory he has in his own Name | God's Deliverance of us, his Covenant with us, and the Promise he gives to his own People
audit_why: Two wrong choices were just other words for the catechism's three reasons (God's rule, his ownership of us, his zeal for worship), so they are replaced with clearly different reasons, and "hath" is modernized to "has".

question: What is the Reason annexed to the third Commandment?
answer: The Reason annexed to the third Commandment, is, that however the breakers of this Commandment may escape Punishment from Men, yet the Lord our God will not suffer them to escape his Righteous Judgment.
right_choice: Breakers may escape Men's Punishment, but the Lord will not suffer them to escape his Righteous Judgment
wrong_choices: God blessed the Sabbath day and made it holy, having rested on the seventh day | God is jealous, and visits the sins of the fathers on the children of those who hate him | Those who keep it will have long life in the land which the Lord gives them
audit_why: The three wrong choices all repeated the catechism's answer in other words, so I replaced them with the reasons the catechism attaches to the second, fourth and fifth Commandments.

question: How is the Sabbath to be sanctified?
answer: The Sabbath is to be sanctified by a holy Resting all that Day, even from such worldly Employments and Recreations as are lawful on other Days; and spending the whole Time in the Public and Private Exercises of God's Worship, except so much as is to be taken up in the Works of Necessity and Mercy.
right_choice: By holy Resting from worldly Employments, spending the Time in God's Worship, except Works of Necessity and Mercy
wrong_choices: By resting from all work and labor completely on the Sabbath day | By ceasing all activities and remaining completely idle in holy contemplation | By spending the day in prayer and attending church services only
audit_why: No fault found.

question: What is the Reason annexed to the fifth Commandment?
answer: The reason annexed to the fifth Commandment, is a Promise of long Life and Prosperity (as far as it shall serve for God's Glory, and their own Good) to all such as keep this Commandment.
right_choice: A Promise of long Life and Prosperity (as far as it serves God's Glory) to all who keep it
wrong_choices: A Promise of mercy to thousands who love the LORD and keep his commandments | A Reminder that the LORD blessed the Sabbath day and made it holy | A Warning that the LORD will not hold guiltless anyone who misuses his name
audit_why: The three wrong choices all described the same promise of blessing for honoring parents, so they were also right; they are now replaced with reasons or promises tied to other commandments.

question: What is required in the sixth Commandment?
answer: The sixth Commandment requires all lawful endeavors to preserve our own life, and the life of others.
right_choice: All lawful endeavors to preserve our own life, and the life of others
wrong_choices: All lawful endeavors to preserve our own purity, and the chastity of others | All lawful endeavors to promote truth between one person and another | All lawful endeavors to further the wealth and outward estate of ourselves and others
audit_why: The old-style wording ("requireth") was modernized, and the wrong choices that were close to the true answer were replaced with what the seventh, eighth and ninth Commandments require.

question: What is forbidden in the eighth Commandment?
answer: The eighth Commandment forbiddeth whatsoever doth, or may, unjustly hinder our own, or our Neighbour's Wealth, or outward Estate.
right_choice: Whatsoever doth, or may, unjustly hinder our own, or our Neighbour's Wealth, or outward Estate
wrong_choices: All attempts to become wealthy and all worldly possessions and material gain | The desiring of our Neighbour's possessions and all forms of greed and covetousness | Whatsoever doth, or may, unjustly take away our own, or our Neighbour's Life

question: Which is the ninth Commandment?
answer: The ninth Commandment is, "You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor."
right_choice: You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor
wrong_choices: You shall not steal | You shall not commit adultery | You shall not covet your neighbor’s house
audit_why: The answer and choices used old "Thou shalt" wording, and two wrong choices (about lying and spreading rumors) meant nearly the same as the right one, so I used the BSB wording and swapped in the neighboring commandments (steal, adultery, covet).

question: What does every sin deserve?
answer: Every sin deserves God's wrath and curse, both in this life and in the life to come.
right_choice: God's wrath and curse, both in this life and in the life to come
wrong_choices: Only a light correction from God, to bring us back to Him | The loss of some reward, but never God's wrath | Shame before other people, but no judgment from God
audit_why: The catechism wording was old-fashioned and the three wrong choices all nearly matched the right answer, so I modernized the wording and replaced the wrong choices with ones that clearly contradict the teaching.

question: How is the Word made effectual to Salvation?
answer: The Spirit of God maketh the Reading, but especially the Preaching of the Word, an effectual Means of convincing and converting Sinners; and of building them up in Holiness and Comfort through Faith unto Salvation.
right_choice: The Spirit maketh the Preaching of God's Word an effectual Means of convincing and converting Sinners unto Salvation
wrong_choices: The Gospel is made effectual by man's understanding of the Word of God | The Spirit maketh only Prayer and Sacraments effectual for Salvation | The Reading of God's Word is the primary Means of convincing Sinners
audit_why: No fault found.

question: How is the Word to be read and heard, that it may become effectual to Salvation?
answer: That the Word may become effectual to Salvation, we must attend thereunto with Diligence, Preparation, and Prayer; receive it with Faith and Love, lay it up in our Hearts, and practice it in our Lives.

question: What does the Preface of the Lord's Prayer teach us?
answer: The Preface of the Lord's Prayer, which is, "Our Father in heaven," teaches us to draw near to God with all holy reverence and confidence, as children to a Father, able and ready to help us; and that we should pray with and for others.

wrong_choices: To recognize God as the sovereign ruler over all creation and all nations | To confess our sins and ask forgiveness through Christ's intercession before God | To acknowledge God's holiness and recognize our unworthiness to approach Him
audit_why: The quoted preface used the KJV's "which art" and the question used old forms like "doth" and "teacheth"; these now follow the BSB ("Our Father in heaven") and modern wording, with the teaching unchanged.

question: What do we pray for in the first Petition?
answer: In the first Petition, which is, "Hallowed be Your name," we pray that God would enable us and others to glorify Him in all that by which He makes Himself known; and that He would dispose all things to His own glory.
right_choice: That God would enable us to glorify His name in all by which He makes Himself known and dispose all things to His glory
wrong_choices: That His kingdom would come and His will be done on the earth | That God would protect His name and prevent the misuse of His holy name | That God would reveal His nature fully and make Himself completely known
audit_why: The catechism's quotation of the petition used the older "thy Name" and "maketh" wording, so it now follows the BSB ("hallowed be Your name") and modern wording, and the right choice matches the style of the wrong ones.

question: Who is the First and Chiefest Being?
answer: God is the First and Chiefest Being

wrong_choices: The world is the First and Chiefest Being | Man is the First and Chiefest Being | The angels are the First and Chiefest Beings

question: Ought every One to believe there is a God?
answer: Every One ought to believe there is a God; and it is their great Sin and Folly who do not.

question: How may we know there is a God?
answer: The Light of Nature in Man, and the Works of God plainly declare there is a God; but his Word and Spirit only, do it fully and effectually, for the Salvation of Sinners.
right_choice: The Light of Nature and God's Works declare there is a God; but his Word and Spirit do it fully and effectually for Salvation
wrong_choices: The Light of Nature and God's Works alone lead sinners fully and effectually to salvation | Through reason and philosophy alone, or through Scripture without the Spirit's work | The works of creation clearly show God's existence equally to every person
audit_why: One wrong choice ("Only through Scripture and the Holy Spirit...") nearly repeats the catechism's own teaching that Word and Spirit alone give full knowledge, so it was replaced with a choice that wrongly says nature alone saves.

question: What is the Word of God?
answer: The Holy Scriptures of the Old and New Testaments are the Word of God, and the only certain Rule of Faith and Obedience.
right_choice: The Holy Scriptures are the Word of God and the only certain Rule of Faith and Obedience
wrong_choices: Scripture is the Word of God, and the Church interprets it for us | The Scriptures contain the Word of God and are our guide for living | The Old and New Testaments, along with Church Tradition, are the Rule of Faith

question: May all Men make use of the Holy Scriptures?
answer: All Men are not only permitted, but commanded and exhorted, to read, hear, and understand the Holy Scriptures.

question: What things are chiefly contained in the Holy Scriptures?
answer: The Holy Scriptures chiefly contain, what Man ought to believe concerning God, and what Duty God requireth of Man.

question: What special Act of Providence did God exercise towards Man in the Estate wherein he was created?
answer: When God had created Man, he entered into a Covenant of Life with him, upon Condition of perfect Obedience: forbidding him to eat of the Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil, upon pain of Death.

question: What is the Misery of that Estate whereinto Man fell?
answer: All Mankind by their Fall lost Communion with God, are under his Wrath and Curse; and so made liable to all Miseries in this Life, to Death it self, and to the Pains of Hell for ever.

question: Did God leave all Mankind to perish in the Estate of Sin and Misery?
answer: God, having out of his meer good pleasure, from all Eternity, elected some to Everlasting Life, did enter into a Covenant of Grace, to deliver them out of the Estate of Sin and Misery, and to bring them into an Estate of Salvation by a Redeemer.
right_choice: God from all Eternity elected some to Everlasting Life and made a Covenant of Grace to deliver them from Sin and Misery by a Redeemer

question: Who is the Redeemer of God's Elect?
answer: The only Redeemer of God's Elect, is the Lord Jesus Christ; who being the Eternal Son of God, became Man, and so was; and continueth to be God and Man, in two distinct Natures, and one Person for ever.
right_choice: The Lord Jesus Christ, the Eternal Son of God who became Man, being God and Man in two distinct Natures and one Person forever
wrong_choices: Christ, God's chosen instrument, who was human like us in all respects | Christ, the mediator between God and humans, truly human but not truly divine | Christ, a created being, the first and highest of all God's creatures

question: Wherein did Christ's Humiliation consist?
answer: Christ's Humiliation consisted in his being born, and that in a low Condition; made under the Law, undergoing the Miseries of this Life, the Wrath of God, and the cursed Death of the Cross; in being buried, and continuing under the Power of Death for a time.

wrong_choices: His resurrection in glory, His ascension to heaven, and His sitting at the right hand of God the Father. | His exercise of prophetic, priestly, and kingly offices with power over all things in heaven and on earth. | His coming again in glory to judge the world at the last day.

question: Wherein consisteth Christ's Exaltation?

question: How does the Spirit apply to us the Redemption purchased by Christ?
answer: The Spirit applies to us the Redemption purchased by Christ, by working Faith in us, and thereby uniting us to Christ, in our effectual Calling.

audit_why: The answer had a printing error ("Chrift") and old wording, and two wrong choices were really the same as the right answer, so I corrected the spelling and wording and replaced those two choices with other benefits of redemption (justification and glorification).

question: What is Justification?
answer: Justification is an Act of God's free Grace, wherein he pardoneth all our Sins, and accepteth us as Righteous in his sight, only for the Righteousness of Christ imputed to us, and received by Faith alone.
right_choice: God's free Grace pardoning all our sins and accepting us as Righteous through Christ's imputed Righteousness, received by Faith alone.
wrong_choices: Christ living a perfect life as our example, so we might follow His pattern and attain righteousness through imitation. | God making us inwardly holy and renewed through the transforming work of the Holy Spirit in progressive sanctification. | God accepting us on the basis of our sincere repentance and our works of obedience to the Law.

question: What Benefits do Believers receive from Christ at their Death?

question: What Benefits do Believers receive from Christ at the Resurrection?
answer: At the Resurrection Believers being raised up in Glory, shall be openly acknowledged, and acquitted in the Day of Judgement, and made perfectly blessed, both in Soul and Body, in the full enjoyment of God, to all Eternity.

question: But what shall be done to the Wicked at their Death?

question: What shall be done to the Wicked at the Day of Judgment?

question: What is the Sum of the Ten Commandments?

question: What is forbidden in the first Commandment?
answer: The first commandment forbids denying, or not worshipping and glorifying, the true God as God and our God, and giving to any other the worship and glory that are due to him alone.

question: Which is the second Commandment?

question: What is required in the third Commandment?
answer: The third Commandment requireth, the Holy and Reverent Use of God's Names, Titles, Attributes, Ordinances, Word, and Works.

question: What is forbidden in the third Commandment?

question: Which is the fourth Commandment?

question: What is required in the fourth Commandment?

question: Which Day of the Seven has God appointed to be the Weekly Sabbath?

question: What is forbidden in the fourth Commandment?

question: What are the Reasons annexed to the fourth Commandment?
answer: The Reasons annexed to the fourth Commandment, are God's allowing us six Days of the Week for our own lawful Employments, his challenging a special Propriety in a Seventh, his own Example, and his blessing the Sabbath Day.
right_choice: God's allowing six days for lawful employments, claiming the seventh, his example, and blessing.
wrong_choices: The sixth day being the Sabbath and God claiming the seventh for people's employments. | God's demanding constant labour six days and rest only for a portion of seventh. | God's forbidding work during the six days and allowing work only on seventh day.

question: Which is the fifth Commandment?
answer: The fifth Commandment is, "Honor your father and mother, so that your days may be long in the land that the LORD your God is giving you."
right_choice: Honor your father and mother, so that your days may be long in the land.
wrong_choices: You shall not murder. | You shall not commit adultery. | Remember the Sabbath day by keeping it holy.
audit_why: The answer and choices used old KJV-style wording ("thy", "thou shalt", "give it thee"), so they now use the Berean Standard Bible wording of Exodus 20:12-14 and 20:8.

question: What is required in the fifth Commandment?
answer: The fifth Commandment requireth the preserving the Honour, and performing the Duties belonging to every one in their several Places and Relations, as Superiours, Inferiors, or Equals.
right_choice: Requireth preserving honour and performing duties in their several places and relations.
wrong_choices: Requireth receiving, observing, and keeping pure all the worship and ordinances God hath appointed in his Word. | Requireth holy and reverent use of God's names, titles, attributes, and ordinances. | Requireth the omission and careless performance of duties during the Sabbath day.

question: What is forbidden in the fifth Commandment?
answer: The fifth Commandment forbiddeth the neglecting of, or doing any thing against the Honor and Duty which belongeth to every one in their several Places and Relations.
right_choice: Forbiddeth neglecting or doing anything against honour and duty in places and relations.
wrong_choices: Requireth preserving honour and performing the duties belonging to every one in relations. | Forbiddeth denying or not worshipping of the true God alone in all things. | Forbiddeth taking God's name in vain or swearing by it falsely.
audit_why: No fault found.

question: What is the sixth Commandment?
answer: The sixth Commandment is, "You shall not murder."
right_choice: The sixth Commandment is, "You shall not murder."
wrong_choices: The sixth Commandment is, "You shall love your neighbor as yourself." | The sixth Commandment is, "You shall not steal." | The sixth Commandment is, "You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor."
audit_why: The answer and choices used old KJV wording ("Thou shalt not kill"), so they were changed to the BSB wording, "You shall not murder," with matching modern wording in the wrong choices.

question: What is forbidden in the sixth Commandment?
answer: The sixth Commandment absolutely forbiddeth the taking away of our own Life; or the Life of our Neighbor unjustly, or whatsoever tendeth thereunto.
right_choice: Absolutely forbiddeth taking away our own life or our neighbor's life unjustly.
wrong_choices: Forbiddeth whatsoever is prejudicial to truth or injurious to neighbor's good name. | Forbiddeth all profaning and abusing of any thing whereby God makes himself known. | Forbiddeth all unchaste thoughts, words and actions of any kind whatsoever.

question: What is required in the seventh Commandment?
answer: The seventh Commandment requireth the preservation of our own and our neighbor's chastity, in heart, speech, and behavior.
right_choice: Requireth preservation of our own and our neighbor's chastity in heart, speech, and behavior.
wrong_choices: Requireth full contentment with our own condition and charitable frame toward neighbor. | Requireth maintaining and promoting truth between man and man, and the good name of our neighbor. | Requireth lawful procuring and furthering the wealth and outward estate of ourselves.
audit_why: The answer had a typo ("out" for "our"), the right choice left out "speech", and one wrong choice (what the commandment forbids) was too close to the right answer, so I fixed the typo, restored "speech", and swapped that choice for a line from the ninth commandment.

question: What is forbidden in the seventh Commandment?
answer: The seventh Commandment forbiddeth all unchast Thoughts, Words and Actions.
right_choice: The seventh Commandment forbiddeth all unchast Thoughts, Words and Actions.
wrong_choices: Forbiddeth whatsoever is prejudicial to truth or injurious to neighbor's good name. | Forbiddeth taking away of our own or our neighbor's life unjustly. | Requireth preservation of our own and our neighbor's chastity in heart and behaviour.
audit_why: No fault found.

question: What is required in the eighth Commandment?
answer: The eighth Commandment requireth the lawful procuring, and furthering the Wealth and outward Estate of our selves, and others.

question: What is required in the ninth Commandment?
answer: The ninth Commandment requireth the maintaining and promoting of Truth between Man and Man, and of our own and our Neighbor's good Name, especially in Witness-bearing.

audit_why: No fault found.

question: What is forbidden in the ninth Commandment?
answer: The ninth Commandment forbiddeth whatsoever is prejudicial to Truth, or injurious to our own or our Neighbor's good name.
right_choice: Forbiddeth whatsoever is prejudicial to truth or injurious to neighbor's good name.
wrong_choices: Requireth maintaining truth between man and man and of our neighbor's good name. | Forbiddeth discontentment with our own estate or envying the good of neighbor. | Forbiddeth taking away of our neighbor's life or whatsoever tendeth thereunto.
audit_why: No fault found.

question: Which is the tenth Commandment?
answer: The tenth Commandment is, "You shall not covet your neighbor’s house. You shall not covet your neighbor’s wife, or his manservant or maidservant, or his ox or donkey, or anything that belongs to your neighbor."
right_choice: You shall not covet your neighbor’s house, wife, servants, animals, or anything that belongs to your neighbor.
wrong_choices: You shall not commit adultery. | You shall not steal. | You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.

question: What is required in the tenth Commandment?
answer: The tenth Commandment requireth the full Contentment with our own Condition, with a right and charitable frame of Spirit toward our Neighbor, and all that is his.
right_choice: Requireth full contentment with our own condition and charitable frame toward neighbor.
wrong_choices: Requireth maintaining and promoting truth between man and man, and our neighbor's good name. | Requireth lawful procuring and furthering the wealth and outward estate of others. | Requireth preservation of our own and our neighbor's chastity in all ways.

question: What is forbidden in the tenth Commandment?
answer: The tenth Commandment forbiddeth all Discontentment with our own Estate; envying or grieving at the Good of our Neighbor, and all inordinate Motions and Affections to any thing that is his.
right_choice: Forbiddeth discontentment with our own estate, envying the good of neighbor.
wrong_choices: Forbiddeth neglecting honour and doing anything against duty in their places. | Forbiddeth whatsoever is prejudicial to truth or injurious to neighbor's good name. | Requireth full contentment with our own condition and charitable frame toward neighbor.
audit_why: No fault found.

question: Is any Man able perfectly to keep the Commandments of God?
answer: No meer Man since the Fall, is able in this Life, perfectly to keep the Commandments of God, but doth daily break them, in Thought, Word, and Deed.
right_choice: No mere man since the fall is able to keep God's commandments perfectly.
wrong_choices: Some men can perfectly keep the commandments through their own righteous efforts. | All men are able to keep the commandments perfectly if they try hard. | Believers in Christ are able to perfectly keep God's commandments in this life.
audit_why: The teaching and the choices are right, but the answer had "Thought, Work, or Deed" where the catechism has "Thought, Word, and Deed", so I corrected that wording.

question: What doth God require of us, that we may escape his Wrath and Curse, due to us for Sin?
answer: To escape the Wrath and Curse of God due to us for Sin, God requireth of us Faith in Jesus Christ, Repentance unto Life, with the diligent use of all the outward Means, whereby Christ communicateth to us the Benefits of Redemption.
right_choice: Faith in Jesus Christ, repentance unto life, and diligent use of means.
wrong_choices: Mere intellectual knowledge of God without faith in Christ or actual repentance. | Works and good deeds alone, without faith in Christ or repentance required. | Strict obedience to the law and perfect works to escape God's wrath.

question: What is Repentance unto Life?
answer: Repentance unto Life is a saving Grace, whereby a Sinner, out of a true Sense of his Sin, and Apprehension of the Mercy of God in Christ, doth, with grief and hatred of his Sin, turn from it unto God, with full Purpose of, and Endeavor after, new Obedience.
right_choice: A saving grace from sense of sin and God's mercy turning to God.
wrong_choices: A saving grace through faith alone without actual turning from sin to God. | Mere emotional sorrow for sin without true turning and purpose for obedience. | Complete freedom from all sin and perfect obedience in this present life.
audit_why: The catechism answer and choices are sound, but the first reference pointed to Acts 11:28 (a famine prophecy) instead of Acts 11:18, which speaks of repentance unto life.

question: What are the outward and ordinary Means, whereby Christ communicateth to us the Benefits of Redemption?
answer: The outward and ordinary Means, whereby Christ communicateth to us the Benefits of Redemption, are his Ordinances, especially the Word, Baptism, the Lord's Supper, and Prayer; all which Means are made effectual to the Elect for Salvation.
right_choice: His ordinances, especially the Word, Baptism, the Lord's Supper, and Prayer.
wrong_choices: Only the sacraments of Baptism and the Lord's Supper alone for salvation. | Good works and religious efforts, by which sinners earn the benefits of redemption. | The preaching of the gospel only, to the exclusion of all sacraments.
audit_why: The answer had a typo ("in ordinary" for "and ordinary"), and the question left out "and ordinary". I fixed both. I also replaced one vague wrong choice with a clearer one: earning redemption by good works.

question: How do Baptism and the Lord's Supper, become effectual Means of Salvation?
answer: Baptism and the Lord's Supper become effectual Means of Salvation, not for any Virtue in them, or in him that doth administer them, but only by the Blessing of Christ, and the working of the Spirit in those that by Faith received them.
right_choice: Not from virtue in them or the minister, but by Christ's blessing.
wrong_choices: By their performance and external participation regardless of faith in Christ. | By spiritual power inherent in the sacraments themselves and in the priest. | Through human effort and obedience without need for Christ's blessing or Spirit.
audit_why: No fault found.

question: What is Baptism?
answer: Baptism is an Ordinance of the New Testament instituted by Jesus Christ, to be unto the Party baptised, a Sign of his Fellowship with him, in his Death, Burial, and Resurrection; of his being ingrafted into him; of Remission of Sins; and of his giving up himself unto God through Jesus Christ, to live and walk in newness of Life.
right_choice: New Testament ordinance instituted by Christ signifying fellowship in death and life.
wrong_choices: A means of salvation through the power of the water and minister. | Old Testament ordinance instituted by Moses signifying the moral law and works. | An optional ceremony with no real spiritual significance to believers in Christ.
audit_why: No fault found.

question: To whom is Baptism to be administered?
answer: Baptism is to be administered to all those, who actually profess Repentance toward God, Faith in, and Obedience to our Lord Jesus Christ, and to none other.
right_choice: To all who actually profess repentance toward God and faith in Christ.
wrong_choices: To all infants and children of believing parents, whether they profess faith. | To all who request it, upon mere intellectual agreement with Christian doctrine. | To all who have been baptized by another church, regardless of faith.
audit_why: No fault found.

question: Are the Infants of such as are Professing Believers to be baptized?
answer: The Infants of such as are professing Believers are not to be baptized, because there is neither Command, or Example in the Holy Scriptures, or certain Consequence from them to baptize such.

question: How is Baptism rightly administered?
answer: Baptism is rightly administered, by Immersion, or dipping the whole Body of the Party in Water, into the Name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, according to Christ's Institution, and the Practice of the Apostles; and not by the sprinkling or pouring of Water, or dipping some Part of the Body, after the Tradition of Men.
right_choice: By immersion or dipping the whole body in water according to Christ's institution.
wrong_choices: By dipping in water but without regard to the name of Trinity. | By sprinkling or pouring water on the head according to church tradition. | By dipping only part of the body in water according to church practice.
audit_why: The catechism answer had a typo ("wore dipping"), which now reads "or dipping"; the teaching, choices and references are sound.

question: What is the Duty of such who are rightly baptized?
answer: It is the Duty of such who are rightly baptized, to give up themselves to some particular and orderly Church of Jesus Christ, that they may walk in all the Commandments and Ordinances of the Lord blameless.

wrong_choices: To join the most popular and culturally dominant church regardless of theology. | To remain independent and not commit to any church in their practice. | To participate in all churches equally without particular commitment to one fellowship.
audit_why: No fault found.

question: What is the Lord's Supper?
answer: The Lord's Supper is an Ordinance of the New Testament instituted by Jesus Christ; wherein by giving and receiving Bread and Wine, according to his Appointment, his Death is shewed forth; and the worthy Receivers are, not after a Corporal and Carnal manner, but by Faith, made Partakers of his Body and Blood, with all his Benefits, to their spiritual Nourishment, and growth in Grace.

question: Who are the proper Subjects of this Ordinance?
answer: They who have been baptized upon a personal Profession of their Faith in Jesus Christ, and Repentance from dead Works.
right_choice: They who have been baptized upon a personal Profession of their Faith in Jesus Christ, and Repentance from dead Works
wrong_choices: Believers alone; baptism is not required for worthy participation in communion | All baptized believers regardless of their current faith profession or repentance | Only those who make public profession and demonstrate mature spiritual sanctification
audit_why: No fault found.

question: What is required to the worthy receiving of the Lord's Supper?
answer: It is required of them that would worthily partake of the Lord's Supper, that they examine themselves, of their Knowledge to discern the Lord's Body, of their Faith to feed upon him, of their Repentance, Love, and new Obedience; lest coming unworthily, they eat and drink Judgment to themselves.

question: What is Prayer?
answer: Prayer is an offering up our Desires to God, by the Assistance of the Holy Spirit, for things agreeable to his Will, in the Name of Christ believing, with Confession of our Sins, and thankful Acknowledgment of his Mercies.

question: What rule has God given for our direction in prayer?
answer: The whole Word of God is of use to direct us in prayer; but the special rule of direction is that prayer which Christ taught his disciples, commonly called the Lord's Prayer.

question: What do we pray for in the Second Petition?

question: What do we pray for in the third Petition?

question: What does the Conclusion of the Lord's Prayer teach?
answer: The Conclusion of the Lord's Prayer, "For Yours is the kingdom and the power and the glory forever. question: What is God?

question: How are we made partakers of the redemption purchased by Christ?

question: What is adoption?

question: Which is the first commandment?

question: What are the reasons annexed to the fourth commandment?

question: Are all transgressions of the law equally heinous?

question: What do we pray for in the second petition?
answer: In the second petition, which is "Thy kingdom come," we pray that satan's kingdom may be destroyed, and that the kingdom of grace may be advanced; ourselves and others brought into it, and kept in it, and that the kingdom of glory may be hastened.

question: What do we pray for in the third petition?
answer: In the third petition, which is, "Thy will be done in earth as it is in heaven," we pray that God by His grace, would make us able and willing to know, obey, and submit to His will in all things, as the angels do in heaven.

question: What do we pray for in the fourth petition?
answer: In the fourth petition, which is, "Give us this day our daily bread," we pray that of God's free gift, we may receive a competent portion of the good things of this life and enjoy His blessing with them.

question: What do we pray for in the fifth petition?

question: What do we pray for in the sixth petition?

question: Who is the first and best of beings?

question: What is the chief end of man?

question: How do we know there is a God?
answer: The light of nature in man, and the works of God, plainly declare that there is a God; but His Word and Spirit only, do effectually reveal Him unto us for our salvation.

question: What is the Word of God?
answer: The Scriptures of the Old and New Testaments, being given by divine inspiration, are the Word of God, the only infallible rule of faith and practice.

question: How do we know that the Bible is the Word of God?
answer: The Bible evidences itself to be God's Word by the heavenliness of its doctrine, the unity of its parts, its power to convert sinners and to edify saints; but the Spirit of God only, bearing witness by and with the Scriptures in our hearts, is able fully to persuade us that the Bible is the Word of God.
right_choice: The Spirit of God bearing witness in our hearts persuades us the Bible is God's Word
wrong_choices: We know it because the Bible has been widely read and translated into many languages | The testimony of early church fathers alone confirms the Bible's authority | Scientific evidence and historical research prove the Bible is God's Word
audit_why: One wrong choice said the Bible never contradicts itself, which is close to the catechism's own evidence of "the unity of its parts", so I replaced it with a choice that is clearly wrong.

question: May all men make use of the Scriptures?
answer: All men are not only permitted, but commanded and exhorted, to read, hear, and understand the Scriptures.

question: How many persons are there in the Godhead?
answer: There are three persons in the Godhead, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit; and these three are one God, the same in essence, equal in power and glory.
right_choice: Three persons in the Godhead—Father, Son, Spirit—one God in essence and power
wrong_choices: One divine person manifesting in three different roles—as Father in creation, Son in redemption, Spirit in sanctification of believers | The Father is God; the Son and Spirit are created beings subordinate to the Father's authority and power | Four distinct divine persons unified in authority, the Father, Son, Spirit, and a fourth divine principle or emanation
audit_why: No fault found.

question: What are the decrees of God?
answer: The decrees of God are His eternal purpose, according to the counsel of His will, whereby for His own glory, He has fore-ordained whatsoever comes to pass

question: How does God execute His decrees?
answer: God executes His decrees in the works of creation and providence.
right_choice: God executes His decrees in the works of creation and providence.
wrong_choices: God's decrees are accomplished through human free will and choice | God executes His decrees only through the laws of nature | God's decrees are carried out by angels and spiritual beings alone
audit_why: No fault found.

question: What special act of providence did God exercise towards man, in the estate wherein he was created?
answer: When God had created man, He entered into a covenant of works with him, upon condition of perfect obedience, forbidding him to eat of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, upon pain of death.

question: Wherein consists the sinfulness of that estate whereunto man fell?
answer: The sinfulness of that estate whereunto man fell, consists in the guilt of Adam's first sin, the want of original righteousness, and the corruption of his whole nature, which is commonly called original sin, together with all actual transgressions which proceed from it.

question: What is the misery of that estate whereunto man fell?
answer: All mankind, by their fall lost communion with God, are under His wrath and curse, and 80 made liable to all the miseries of this life, to death itself, and to the pains of hell forever.

question: Did God leave all mankind to perish in the estate of sin and misery?
answer: God, out of His mere good pleasure, from all eternity, having chosen a people to everlasting life, did enter into a covenant of grace, to deliver them out of the estate of sin and misery, and to bring them into an estate of salvation, by a Redeemer.

question: Who is the Redeemer of God's elect?
answer: The only Redeemer of God's elect is the Lord Jesus Christ, who, being the eternal Son of God, became man, and so was and continues to be God and man, in two distinct natures and one person, forever.

question: How did Christ, being the Son of God, become man?
answer: Christ, the Son of God became man by taking to himself a true body and a reasonable soul; being conceived by the power of the Holy Spirit in the womb of the Virgin Mary and born of her, yet without sin.
right_choice: Christ took a true body and soul, conceived by the Holy Spirit and born of Mary
wrong_choices: Christ was born a normal human and later adopted into divine sonship when the Spirit descended at baptism | The eternal Christ-Spirit became human in Jesus while not truly possessing a body or suffering any human limitation | Christ took a human body from Mary but possessed a divine spirit rather than a human soul
audit_why: No fault found.

question: What offices does Christ execute as our Redeemer?
answer: Christ, as our Redeemer, executes the offices of a prophet, of a priest, and of a king, both in His estate of humiliation and exaltation.

question: How does Christ execute the office of a prophet?
answer: Christ executes the office of a prophet, in revealing to us, by this Word and Spirit, the will of God for our salvation.

question: How does Christ execute the office of a priest?
answer: Christ executes the office of a priest, in His once offering up of Himself, a sacrifice to satisfy divine justice, and reconcile us to God, and in making continual intercession for us.

question: How does Christ execute the office of a king?
answer: Christ executes the office of a king, in subduing us to Himself, in ruling and defending us, and in restraining and conquering all His and our enemies.

question: Wherein consists Christ's exaltation?
answer: Christ's exaltation consists in His rising again from the dead on the third day, in ascending up into heaven, in sitting at the right hand of God the Father, and in coming to judge the world at the last day.

question: How does the Spirit apply to us the redemption purchased by Christ?
answer: The Spirit applies to us the redemption purchased by Christ, by working faith in us, and thereby uniting us to Christ in our effectual calling.

question: What is effectual calling?
answer: Effectual calling is the work of God's Spirit, whereby, convincing us of our sin and misery, enlightening our minds in the knowledge of Christ, and renewing our wills, He does persuade and enable us to embrace Jesus Christ, freely offered to us in the Gospel.

question: What benefits do they that are effectually called, partake of in this life?
answer: They that are effectually called, do in this life partake of justification, adoption, sanctification, and the several benefits which in this life do either accompany or flow from them.
right_choice: They partake of justification, adoption, sanctification, and the several benefits which accompany or flow from them
wrong_choices: They partake of justification and adoption only | They partake of sanctification and perseverance in grace only | They partake of grace and assurance only
audit_why: The catechism answer is right, but one wrong choice (sanctification and perseverance) was partly true, and the wrong choices were longer than the right one, so I added "only" and made all the choices short and parallel.

question: What is justification?
answer: Justification is an act of God's free grace, wherein He pardons all our sins, and accepts us as righteous in His sight, only for the righteousness of Christ imputed to us, and received by faith alone.

question: What is sanctification?
answer: Sanctification is a work of God's free grace whereby we are renewed in the whole man after the image of God, and are enabled more and more to die unto sin, and live unto righteousness.

question: What are the benefits which in this life do accompany or flow from justification, adoption, and sanctification?
answer: The benefits which in this life do accompany or flow from justification, adoption, and sanctification, are, assurance of God's love, peace of conscience, joy in the Holy Spirit, increase of grace, and perseverance therein to the end.
right_choice: Assurance of God's love, peace of conscience, joy in the Holy Spirit, increase of grace, and perseverance
wrong_choices: Wealth and earthly prosperity, good health, long life, and protection from all suffering and trial. | Visible miracles and supernatural powers, special revelations, and clear signs of God's favor. | Freedom from all temptation, complete moral perfection, and victory over every human weakness.
audit_why: No fault found.

question: What benefits do believers receive from Christ at death?
answer: The souls of believers are at death made perfect in holiness, and do immediately pass into glory, and their bodies, being still united to Christ, do rest in their graves till the resurrection.

question: What benefits do believers receive from Christ at the Resurrection?
answer: At the resurrection, believers become raised up in glory, shall be openly acknowledged and acquitted in the day of judgment, and made perfectly blessed in the full enjoyment of God to all eternity.

question: What shall be done to the wicked at death?
answer: The souls of the wicked shall at death, be cast into the torments of hell, and their bodies lie in their graves till the resurrection and judgement of the great day.

question: What shall be done to the wicked at the day of judgement?
answer: At the day of judgement, the bodies of the wicked, being raised out of their graves, shall be sentenced, together with their souls, to unspeakable torments with the devil and his angels forever.

question: What is the duty which God requires of man?
answer: The duty which God requires of man, is obedience to His revealed will.
right_choice: God requires man's obedience to His revealed will
wrong_choices: To strive to do whatever makes us happy and fulfilled | To obey the moral law we discover through our own reason | To follow the teachings of religious leaders and traditions
audit_why: No fault found.

question: Where is the moral law summarily comprehended?
answer: The moral law is summarily comprehended in the Ten Commandments.
right_choice: The moral law is summarily comprehended in the Ten Commandments.
wrong_choices: The moral law is found in the ceremonial laws of the Old Testament | The moral law is summarized in the Sermon on the Mount | The moral law is revealed through nature and human conscience alone
audit_why: No fault found.

question: What is the sum of the Ten Commandments?
answer: The sum of the Ten Commandments is, to love the Lord our God, with all our heart, with all our soul, with all our strength, and with all our mind; and our neighbor as ourselves.

question: What is the preface to the Ten Commandments?
answer: The preface to the Ten Commandments is, "I am the Lord thy God, which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage."

question: What does the preface to the Ten Commandments teach us?
answer: The preface to the Ten Commandments teaches us, that because God is the Lord, and our God and Redeemer, therefore we are bound to keep all His commandments.

question: What is required in the first commandment?
answer: The first commandment requires us to know and acknowledge God to be the only true God, and our God, and to worship and glorify Him accordingly.

question: What is forbidden in the first commandment?
answer: The first commandment forbids the denying, or not worshipping and glorifying the true God, as God and our God; and the giving that worship and glory to any other, which is due unto Him alone.

question: What are we especially taught by these words, "before me," in the first commandment?
answer: These words, "before me", in the first commandment, teach us, that God, who sees all things, takes notice of, and is much displeased with the sin of having any other God.

question: Which is the second commandment?
answer: The second commandment is, "Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, or any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth. Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them; for I the Lord thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me: and showing mercy unto thousands of them that love me and keep my commandments."

question: What is required in the second commandment?
answer: The second commandment requires the receiving, observing, and keeping pure and entire, all such religious worship and ordinances, as God has appointed in His Word.

question: What is forbidden in the second commandment?
answer: The second commandment forbids the worshipping of God by images, or any other way not appointed in His Word.

question: What are the reasons annexed to the second commandment?
answer: The reasons annexed to the second commandment, are, God's sovereignty over us, His propriety in us, and the zeal He has for His own worship.

question: What is required in the third commandment?
answer: The third commandment requires the holy and reverent use of God's names, titles, attributes, ordinances, words, and works.

question: What is forbidden in the third commandment?
answer: The third commandment forbids all profaning and abusing of any thing whereby God makes Himself known.

question: What is the reason annexed to the third commandment?
answer: The reason annexed to the third commandment is, that howsoever the breakers of this commandment may escape punishment from men, yet the Lord our God will not suffer them to escape His righteous judgment.

question: Which is the fourth commandment?
answer: The fourth commandment is, "Remember the Sabbath day to keep it holy. Six days shalt thou labor and do all thy work; but the seventh day is the Sabbath of the Lord thy God: in it thou shalt not do any work, thou, nor thy son, nor thy daughter, thy manservant, nor thy maid servant, nor thy cattle, nor thy stranger that is within thy gates: for in six days the Lord made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that in them is, and rested the seventh day: wherefore the Lord blessed the Sabbath day and hallowed it."

question: What is required in the fourth commandment?
answer: The fourth commandment requires the keeping holy to God such set times as He has appointed in His Word, expressly one whole day in seven to be a holy Sabbath to Himself.

question: Which day of the seven has God appointed to be the weekly Sabbath?
answer: From the creation of the world to the resurrection of Christ, God appointed the seventh day of the week to be the weekly Sabbath; and the first day of the week ever since, to continue to the end of the world, which is the Christian Sabbath.

question: How is the Sabbath to be sanctified?
answer: The Sabbath is to sanctified by a holy resting all that day, even from such worldly employments and recreations as are lawful on other days, and spending the time in the public and private exercises of God's worship, except so much as is to be taken up in the works of necessity and mercy.

question: What is forbidden in the fourth commandment?
answer: The fourth commandment forbids the omission or careless performance of the duties required, and the profaning the day by idleness, or doing that which is in itself sinful, or by unnecessary thoughts, words, or works, about worldly employments or recreations.

question: What is required in the fifth commandment?
answer: The fifth commandment requires the preserving the honor, and performing the duties, belonging to every one in their several places and relations, as superiors, inferiors, or equals.

question: What is forbidden in the fifth commandment?
answer: The fifth commandment forbids the neglecting of, or doing anything against the honor and duty which belongs to every one in their several places and relations.

question: What is the reason annexed to the fifth commandment?
answer: The reason annexed to the fifth commandment is a promise of long life and prosperity (as far as it shall serve God's glory and their own good), to all such as keep this commandment.

question: What is required in the sixth commandment?
answer: The sixth commandment requires all lawful endeavors to preserve our own life and the life of others.

question: What is forbidden in the sixth commandment?
answer: The sixth commandment forbids the taking away our own life, or the life of our neighbor unjustly, or whatsoever tends thereto.

question: What is required in the seventh commandment?
answer: The seventh commandment requires the preservation of our own and our neighbor's chastity, in heart, speech, and behavior.

question: What is forbidden in the seventh commandment?
answer: The seventh commandment forbids all unchaste thoughts, words, and actions.

question: What is required in the eighth commandment?
answer: The eighth commandment requires the lawful procuring and furthering the wealth and outward state of ourselves and others.

question: What is forbidden in the eighth commandment?
answer: The eighth commandment forbids whatsoever does or may unjustly hinder our own or our neighbor's wealth or outward state.

question: What is required in the ninth commandment?
answer: The ninth commandment requires the maintaining and promoting of truth between man and man, and of our own and our neighbor's good name, especially in witness bearing.

question: What is forbidden in the ninth commandment?
answer: The ninth commandment forbids whatsoever is pre- judicial to truth, or injurious to our own, or our neighbor's good name.

question: Which is the tenth commandment?
answer: The tenth commandment is, "Thou shalt not covet thy neighbor's house. Thou shalt not covet thy neighbor's wife, nor his man servant, nor his maid servant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor anything that is thy neighbor's."

question: What is required in the tenth commandment?
answer: The tenth commandment requires full contentment with our own condition, with a right and charitable frame of spirit towards our neighbor, and all that is his.

question: What is forbidden in the tenth commandment?
answer: The tenth commandment forbids all discontentment with our own estate, envying or grieving at the good of our neighbor, and all inordinate motions and affections to anything that is his.

question: Is any man able perfectly to keep the commandments of God?
answer: No mere man, since the fall, is able in this life, perfectly to keep the commandments of God, but daily breaks them in thought, word, and deed.

question: What then is the purpose of the law since the fall?
answer: The purpose of the law, since, the fall, is to reveal the perfect righteousness of God, that His people may know his will for their lives and the ungodly, being convicted of their sin, may be restrained therein and brought to Christ for salvation.
right_choice: To reveal God's perfect righteousness so His people know His will and ungodly are convicted
wrong_choices: To demonstrate that human effort and obedience can achieve the righteousness required by God | To show God's hatred of sinners and to condemn unbelievers to eternal punishment | To prepare people for salvation by removing sins through perfect obedience to God's commands
audit_why: No fault found.

question: What does every sin deserve?
answer: Every sin deserves God's wrath and curse, both in this life, and in that which is to come.

question: What does God require of us, that we may escape His wrath and curse, due to us for sin?
answer: To escape the wrath and curse of God due to us for sin, God requires of us faith in Jesus Christ, repentance unto life, with the diligent use of all the outward and ordinary means whereby Christ communicates to us the benefits of redemption.

question: What is repentance unto life?
answer: Repentance unto life is a saving grace, whereby a sinner, out of a true sense of his sin, and apprehension of the mercy of God in Christ, does, with grief and hatred of his sin, turn from it unto God, with full purpose of, and endeavor after, new obedience.

question: What are the outward and ordinary means whereby Christ communicates to us the benefits of redemption?
answer: The outward and ordinary means whereby Christ communicates to us the benefits of redemption are His ordinances, especially the Word, Baptism, the Lord's Supper and Prayer; all which are made effectual to the elect for salvation.

question: How is the Word made effectual to salvation?
answer: The Spirit of God makes the reading, but especially the preaching of the Word an effectual means of convincing and converting sinners, and of building them up in holiness and comfort, through faith unto salvation.

question: How is the Word to be read and heard that it may become effectual to salvation?
answer: That the Word may become effectual to salvation we must attend thereunto with diligence, preparation and prayer, receive it in faith and love, lay it up in our hearts and practice it in our lives.

question: How do Baptism and the Lord's Supper become effectual means of salvation?
answer: Baptism and the Lord's Supper become effectual means of salvation, not from any virtue in them or in him that administers them, but only by the blessing of Christ and the working of His Spirit in them that by faith receive them.

question: Wherein do Baptism and the Lord's Supper differ from the other ordinances of God?
answer: Baptism and the Lord's Supper differ from the other ordinances of God in that they were specially instituted by Christ to represent and apply to believers the benefits of the new covenant by visible and outward signs.
right_choice: Specially instituted by Christ to represent and apply to believers benefits of the new covenant
wrong_choices: Established by church councils as tests of faith and loyalty to Christian authority | Commanded by God in the Old Testament as signs of judgment for sin | Created by church tradition to symbolize spiritual truths without conferring any real grace to believers
audit_why: No fault found.

question: What is Baptism?
answer: Baptism is an holy ordinance, wherein the washing with water in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, signifies our ingrafting into Christ and partaking of the benefits of the covenant of grace, and our engagement to be the Lord's.

question: To whom is Baptism to be administered?
answer: Baptism is to be administered to all those who actually profess repentance towards God, faith in, and obedience to our Lord Jesus Christ; and to none other.

question: Are the infants of such as are professing believers to be baptized?
answer: The infants of such as are professing believers are not to be baptized; because there is neither command nor example in the Holy Scriptures, or certain consequence from them, to baptize such.

question: How is Baptism rightly administered?
answer: Baptism is rightly administered by immersion, or dipping the whole body of the person in water, in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.

question: What is the duty of those who are rightly baptized?
answer: It is the duty of those who are rightly baptized to give up (join) themselves to some visible and orderly church of Jesus Christ, that they may walk in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless.

question: What is the visible church?
answer: The visible church is the organized society of professing believers, in all ages and places, wherein the Gospel is truly preached and the ordinances of Baptism and the Lord's Supper rightly administered.
right_choice: The organized society of professing believers where the Gospel is truly preached and ordinances rightly administered
wrong_choices: The universal congregation of all believers throughout history who have true faith, regardless of doctrine or practice | A social organization dedicated to moral improvement and community service in the name of Christian faith and ideals | An institution governed by church leaders whose traditions and teachings guide believers in their understanding of Scripture
audit_why: No fault found.

question: What is the Lord's Supper?
answer: The Lord's Supper is a holy ordinance, wherein, by giving and receiving bread and wine, according to Christ's appointment, His death is showed forth, and the worthy receivers are, not after a corporeal and carnal manner, but by faith, made partakers of His body and blood, with all His benefits, to their spiritual nourishment, and growth in grace.

question: What is required to the worthy receiving of the Lord's Supper?
answer: It is required of them that would worthily (that is, suitably) partake of the Lord's Supper, that they examine themselves, of their knowledge to discern the Lord's body; of their faith to feed upon Him; of their repentance, love, and new obedience: lest, coming unworthily, they eat and drink judgment to themselves.

question: What is Prayer?
answer: Prayer is an offering up of our desires to God, for things agreeable to His will, in the name of Christ, with confession of our sins and thankful acknowledgment of His mercies.

question: What rule has God given for our direction in prayer?
answer: The whole Word of God is of use to direct us in prayer, but the special rule of direction is that prayer, which Christ taught His disciples, commonly called the Lord's Prayer.

question: What does the preface of the Lord's Prayer teach us?
answer: The preface of the Lord's Prayer, which is, "Our Father, which art in heaven," teaches us to draw near to God, with all holy reverence and confidence, as children to a father, able and ready to help us, and that we should pray with and for others.

question: What do we pray for in the first petition?
answer: In the first petition, which is "Hallowed be thy name," we pray that God would enable us and others to glorify Him in all that whereby He makes Himself known, and that He would dispose all things to His own glory.

question: What does the conclusion of the Lord's Prayer teach us?
answer: The conclusion of the Lord's Prayer, which is, "For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, forever, Amen," teaches us to take our encouragement in prayer from God only, and in our prayers to praise Him, ascribing kingdom, power, and glory to Him; and in testimony of our desire, and assurance to be heard, we say, AMEN.

question: What is God?
answer: God is Spirit, infinite, eternal, and unchangeable, in his being, wisdom, power, holiness, justice, goodness and truth.

question: What are the decrees of God?
answer: The decrees of God are his eternal purpose according to the counsel of his own will, whereby for his own glory he has foreordained whatever comes to pass.

question: What is the work of creation?
answer: The work of creation is God's making all things of nothing, by the Word of his power, in six normal consecutive days, and all very good.

question: What special act of providence did God exercise toward man in the state wherein he was created?
answer: When God had created man, he entered into a covenant of life with him, upon condition of perfect obedience, forbidding him to eat of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, upon pain of death.

question: Did our first parents continue in the state wherein they were created?
answer: Our first parents being left to the freedom of their own will, fell from the state wherein they were created, by sinning against God by eating the forbidden fruit.

question: What is sin?
answer: Sin is any want of conformity to, or transgression of the law of God.

question: Into what estate did the fall bring mankind?
answer: The fall brought mankind into a state of sin and misery.

question: Wherein consists the sinfulness of that state whereinto man fell?
answer: The sinfulness of that state whereinto man fell, consists in the guilt of Adam's first sin, the want of original righteousness, and the corruption of his whole nature, which is commonly called original sin, together with all actual transgressions which proceed from it.

question: What is the misery of that state whereinto man fell?
answer: All mankind, by their fall, lost communion with God, are under his wrath and curse, and so made liable to all the miseries in this life, to death itself, and to the pains of hell for ever.

question: Did God leave all mankind to perish in the state of sin and misery?
answer: God having, out of his good pleasure from all eternity, elected some to everlasting life did enter into a covenant of grace to deliver them out of the state of sin and misery, and to bring them into a state of salvation by a Redeemer.

question: Who is the Redeemer of God's elect?
answer: The only Redeemer of God's elect is the Lord Jesus Christ, who being the eternal Son of God, became man and so was and continues to be God and man, in two distinct natures and one person for ever.

question: How did Christ, being the Son of God, become man?
answer: Christ, the son of God, became man by taking to himself a true body and a reasonable soul, being conceived by the power of the Holy Spirit in the Virgin Mary, and born of her yet without sin.

question: What offices does Christ execute as our Redeemer?
answer: Christ as our Redeemer executes the offices of a prophet, of a priest, and of a king, both in his state of humiliation and exaltation.

question: How does Christ execute the office of a prophet?
answer: Christ executes the office of a prophet, in revealing to us, by his Word, and Spirit, the will of God for our salvation.

question: How does Christ execute the office of a priest?
answer: Christ executes the office of a priest, in his once offering up himself a sacrifice to satisfy divine justice, and to reconcile us to God and in making continual intercession for us.

question: Wherein consists Christ's exaltation?
answer: Christ's exaltation consists in his rising again from the dead on the third day, in ascending up into heaven, and sitting at the right hand of God the Father, and in coming to judge the world at the last day.

question: How does the Spirit apply to us the redemption purchased by Christ?
answer: The Spirit applies to us the redemption purchased by Christ, by working faith in us and by it uniting us to Christ in our effectual calling.

question: What benefits do they who are effectually called, partake of in this life?
answer: They who are effectually called, do in this life partake of justification, adoption, sanctification, and the various benefits which in this life do either accompany, or flow from them.

question: What is sanctification?
answer: Sanctification is the work of God's Spirit whereby we are renewed in the whole man after the image of God and are enabled more and more to die to sin, and live to righteousness.

question: What are the benefits which in this life do either accompany or flow from justification, adoption, and sanctification?
answer: The benefits which in this life do accompany or flow from justification, are assurance of God's love, peace of conscience, joy in the Holy Spirit, increase of grace, perseverance in it to the end.

question: What benefits do believers receive from Christ at their death?
answer: The souls of believers are at their death made perfect in holiness and do immediately pass into glory, and their bodies, being still united to Christ do rest in their graves till the resurrection.

question: What benefits do believers receive from Christ at the resurrection?
answer: At the resurrection, believers being raised up in glory, shall be openly acknowledged and acquitted in the day of judgment, and made perfectly blessed both in soul and body in the full enjoying of God to all eternity.

question: What shall be done to the wicked at their death?
answer: The souls of the wicked shall at their death be cast into the torments of hell, and their bodies lie in their graves till the resurrection and judgment of the great day.

question: What did God reveal to man for the rule of his obedience?
answer: The rule which God first revealed to man for his obedience is the moral law which is summarised in the ten commandments.

question: Which is the second commandment?
answer: The second commandment is, "Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, or any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth: Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I the Lord thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me; and shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments."

question: Which is the third commandment?
answer: You shall not take the name of the LORD your God in vain, for the LORD will not leave anyone unpunished who takes His name in vain.
right_choice: You shall not take the name of the LORD your God in vain.
wrong_choices: You shall not bow down to them or worship them. | You shall have no other gods before Me. | Remember the Sabbath day by keeping it holy.

question: What is required in the third commandment?
answer: The third commandment requires the holy and reverent use of God's names, titles, attributes, ordinances, Word, and works.

question: Which is the fourth commandment?
answer: The fourth commandment is, Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy. Six days shalt thou labour, and do all thy work: but the seventh day is the Sabbath of the Lord thy God: in it thou shalt not do any work, thou, nor thy son, nor thy daughter, thy manservant, nor thy maidservant, nor they cattle, nor thy stranger that is within thy gates. For in six days the Lord made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that in them is, and rested the seventh day: wherefore the Lord blessed the Sabbath day and hallowed it.

question: How is the Sabbath to be sanctified?
answer: The Sabbath is to be sanctified by a holy resting all that day, even from such worldly employments and recreations as are lawful on other days, and spending the whole time in the public and private exercises of God's worship, except so much as is taken up in the works of necessity and mercy.

question: What is required in the fifth commandment?
answer: The fifth commandment requires the preserving the honour, and performing the duties belonging to every one in their various positions and relationships as superiors, inferiors, or equals.

question: What is forbidden in the sixth commandment?
answer: The sixth commandment forbids the taking away of our own life, or the life of our neighbour unjustly, or whatever tends to it.

question: What is forbidden in the eighth commandment?
answer: The eighth commandment forbids whatever does or may unjustly hinder our own or our neighbour's wealth, or outward estate.

question: What is required in the ninth commandment?
answer: The ninth commandment requires the maintaining and promoting of truth between man and man, and of our own, and our neighbour's good name, especially in witness-bearing.

question: What is the tenth commandment?
answer: The tenth commandment is, Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour's house; thou shalt not covet thy neighbour's wife,nor his manservant, or his maidservant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor anything that is thy neighbour's.

question: What is forbidden in the tenth commandment?
answer: The tenth commandment forbids all discontentment with our own estate, envying or grieving at the good of our neighbour, and all inordinate emotions and affections to anything that is his.

question: Is any man able perfectly to keep the commandments of God?
answer: No mere man, since the fall, is able in his life perfectly to keep the commandments of God, but does daily break them in thought, word, and deed.

question: Are all transgressions of the law equally heinous?
answer: Some sins in themselves, and by reason of various aggravations are more heinous in the sight of God than others.

question: What does every sin deserve?
answer: Every sin deserves God's wrath and curse, both in this life and that which is to come.

question: How may we escape his wrath and curse due to us for sin?
answer: To escape the wrath and curse of God due to us for sin, we must believe in the Lord Jesus Christ, trusting alone to his blood and righteousness. This faith is attended by repentance for the past, and leads to holiness in the future.

question: What is faith in Jesus Christ?
answer: Faith in Jesus Christ is a saving grace, whereby we receive, and rest upon him alone for salvation, as he is set forth in the gospel.

question: What is repentance to life?
answer: Repentance to life is a saving grace, whereby a sinner, out of a true sense of his sins, and apprehension of the mercy of God in Christ, does with grief and hatred of his sin turn from it to God, with full purpose to strive after new obedience.

question: What are the outward means whereby the Holy Spirit communicates to us the benefits of redemption?
answer: The outward and ordinary means whereby the Holy Spirit communicates to us the benefits of Christ's redemption, are the Word, by which souls are begotten to spiritual life; Baptism, the Lord's Supper, Prayer, and Meditation, by all which believers are further edified in their most holy faith.

question: How is the Word made effectual to salvation?
answer: The Spirit of God makes the reading, but especially the preaching of the Word, an effectual means of convicting and converting sinners, and of building them up in holiness and comfort, through faith to salvation.

question: How is the Word to be read and heard that it may become effectual to salvation?
answer: That the Word may become effectual to salvation, we must attend to it with diligence, and prayer receive it with faith, and love, lay it up into our hearts, and practise it in our lives.

question: How do Baptism and the Lord's Supper become spiritually helpful?
answer: Baptism and the Lord's Supper become spiritually helpful, not from any virtue in them, or in him who does administer them, but only by the blessing of Christ and the working of the Spirit in those who by faith receive them.

question: What is Baptism?
answer: Baptism is an ordinance of the New Testament, instituted by Jesus Christ to be to the person baptised a sign of his fellowship with him, in his death, and burial, and resurrection, of his being ingrafted into him, of remission of sins, and of his giving up himself to God through Jesus Christ, to live and walk in newness of life.

question: To whom is Baptism to be administered?
answer: Baptism is to be administered to all those who actually profess repentance towards God, and faith in our Lord Jesus Christ, and to none other.

question: Are the infants of such as are professing believers to be baptized?

question: How is baptism rightly administered?

question: What is the duty of such as are rightly baptized?

question: What is the Lord's Supper?

question: What is required to the worthy receiving of the Lord's Supper?

question: Why are some people not Humble?

question: What must we do that we may see our sins and our sinfulnesses?
answer: 1. We must search the Scriptures. 2. We must hear the Word of God Preached. 3. We must Examine our Consciences. 4. We must Pray to God for his Spirit

question: If a poor Creature comes to Christ, crying, lamenting and confessing his sins, will Christ receive him?
answer: YES, YES: His merciful Arms are spread wide open to receive him
right_choice: YES, YES: His merciful Arms are spread wide open to receive him

question: What will the Lord do for such a one that comes to him?
answer: 1. He will Pardon all their sins. 2. He will give them Grace. 3. He will give them Peace. 4. He will Comfort them. 5. He will provide for them. 6. He will take their parts. 7. He will bring them to Heaven
right_choice: He will pardon their sins, grant them grace and peace, comfort them, provide for them, and bring them to Heaven
wrong_choices: Pardon them immediately and sanctify them completely so they need not struggle against sin. | Accept them into His church but delay their eternal rewards until they prove themselves worthy. | Grant them prosperity and protection from earthly troubles, health, and a long and comfortable life.

question: When the Lord has done this for a poor Creature, what must he do for this good God of his?
answer: He must be Humble and Thankful
right_choice: He must be Humble and Thankful
wrong_choices: He must be Strong and Steadfast in faith | He must be Holy and Righteous always | He must be Patient and Obedient forever
audit_why: No fault found.

question: How must he shew himself Humble and Thankful?
answer: He must love the Lord with all his Heart, with all his Soul, and serve the Lord with all his strength, and he must love his Neighbour as himself, and for the Lords sake; and this he must do all the dayes of his Life
right_choice: Love the Lord with all your heart and soul, and love your neighbour as yourself all the days of your life
wrong_choices: Give generously to the poor, serve others humbly, and live a life of self-denial. | Thank God daily in prayer, avoid all sin in thought and action, and keep yourself pure. | Fast and pray often, attend worship every week, and give a tenth of your income to the Lord.

question: Who made you?

question: What else did God make?
wrong_choices: God made only the things we can see | God made only the plants and animals | God made only the things in heaven

question: Why did God make you and all things?
wrong_choices: To test mankind's obedience | To establish His kingdom | For man's happiness
audit_why: The answer matches the catechism and the Bible (people are "created for My glory," and God created all things), but the question had no reference, so Isaiah 43:7 and Revelation 4:11 were added.

question: How can you glorify God?
answer: By loving him and doing what he commands.
right_choice: By loving him and doing what he commands.
wrong_choices: By being rich and respected in the world | By studying theology and philosophy | By doing whatever seems right to us
